title: Slitherlink with a unique solution
description: Generate a Slitherlink puzzle, one of Nikoli's: draw one closed loop along the grid lines so that every number says how many sides of its cell the loop uses. The abstraction guesses a loop of at least len edges and the k cells that show their number (0 to 3); the check looks for two different loops that fit all numbers, and the refinement asks for a number that fails for one of them. That the loop is one loop and not several is a reachability condition, in both solvers. The run stops at the first puzzle.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The grid: cells, vertices, edges and the sides of each cell. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% Slitherlink on an n x n grid of cells: draw one closed loop along the grid lines so that
% a number in a cell says how many of the cell's four sides the loop uses. An instance may
% print numbers pre(R,C,N).
#const n = 5.
cell(R,C) :- R = 1..n, C = 1..n.
vertex(X,Y) :- X = 0..n, Y = 0..n.
% The edges of the grid: h(X,Y) joins vertex X,Y to X,Y+1; v(X,Y) joins X,Y to X+1,Y.
edge(h(X,Y)) :- vertex(X,Y), Y < n.
edge(v(X,Y)) :- vertex(X,Y), X < n.
ends(h(X,Y),(X,Y),(X,Y+1)) :- edge(h(X,Y)).
ends(v(X,Y),(X,Y),(X+1,Y)) :- edge(v(X,Y)).
at(E,P) :- ends(E,P,_).
at(E,P) :- ends(E,_,P).
% The four sides of cell R,C (its corners are the vertices R-1..R, C-1..C).
side(R,C,h(R-1,C-1)) :- cell(R,C).
side(R,C,h(R,C-1)) :- cell(R,C).
side(R,C,v(R-1,C-1)) :- cell(R,C).
side(R,C,v(R-1,C)) :- cell(R,C).
% The vertices in a fixed order, to pick the first vertex of a loop.
next((X,Y),(X,Y+1)) :- vertex(X,Y), Y < n.
next((X,n),(X+1,0)) :- vertex(X,n), X < n.
printed(R,C) :- pre(R,C,_).

fragments.name: rules
fragments.description: One closed loop, for any loop a solver declares; used by solver A (one loop) and solver C (two loops).
fragments.text:
% The rules for every loop G that a solver declares with grid(G):
% on(G,E) says that loop G uses the edge E.
{ on(G,E) : edge(E) } :- grid(G).
% Every vertex has two loop edges or none.
deg(G,P,D) :- grid(G), vertex(X,Y), P = (X,Y), D = #count { E : at(E,P), on(G,E) }.
:- deg(G,P,D), D != 0, D != 2.
% One loop: every vertex on the loop is reachable from the first one along loop edges.
used(G,P) :- deg(G,P,2).
later(G,Q) :- used(G,P), next(P,Q).
later(G,Q) :- later(G,P), next(P,Q).
reach(G,P) :- used(G,P), not later(G,P).
reach(G,Q) :- reach(G,P), on(G,E), at(E,P), at(E,Q).
:- used(G,P), not reach(G,P).
% The loop is not empty.
:- grid(G), not used(G,_).
% Every loop respects the printed numbers.
:- grid(G), pre(R,C,N), #count { E : side(R,C,E), on(G,E) } != N.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a loop and the k cells that show their number.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a loop s of at least len edges and k cells that show their number.
grid(s).
:- #count { E : on(s,E) } < len.
k { clue(R,C) : cell(R,C), not printed(R,C) } k.
% num(R,C,N): the puzzle shows N in cell R,C.
num(R,C,N) :- clue(R,C), N = #count { E : side(R,C,E), on(s,E) }.
% Puzzles show 0..3: a 4 would give the loop away (it is the one around that cell).
:- num(_,_,4).
#show num/3.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the numbers shown. The loop stays private to solver A.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for two different loops that fit the numbers (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: two different loops a and b that fit all numbers shown.
grid(a). grid(b).
:- num(R,C,N), grid(G), #count { E : side(R,C,E), on(G,E) } != N.
differ :- on(a,E), not on(b,E).
differ :- on(b,E), not on(a,E).
:- not differ.
#show.
#show a(E) : on(a,E).
#show b(E) : on(b,E).

% Both loops fit every puzzle that shows only numbers that hold for both. So the puzzle
% must show a number that fails for a or for b.
count(G,R,C,N) :- grid(G), cell(R,C), N = #count { E : side(R,C,E), on(G,E) }.
relevant(num(R,C,N)) :- cell(R,C), N = 0..3, not printed(R,C), not count(a,R,C,N).
relevant(num(R,C,N)) :- cell(R,C), N = 0..3, not printed(R,C), not count(b,R,C,N).

fragments.name: view
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.
fragments.text:
% The corners of the grid as nodes, its lines as edges, the numbers at the cell centres;
% the two loops of a counterexample in colour.
#program scene.
draw(node(p(X,Y))) :- vertex(X,Y).
draw(attr(node(p(X,Y)), label, "")) :- vertex(X,Y).
draw(ghost(node(p(X,Y)))) :- vertex(X,Y).
draw(pos(node(p(X,Y)), Y*1000/n, X*1000/n)) :- vertex(X,Y).
draw(edge(p(X1,Y1),p(X2,Y2))) :- ends(_,(X1,Y1),(X2,Y2)).
draw(node(n(R,C))) :- cell(R,C).
draw(attr(node(n(R,C)), label, "")) :- cell(R,C), not pre(R,C,_), not shown(R,C).
draw(pos(node(n(R,C)), (2*C-1)*500/n, (2*R-1)*500/n)) :- cell(R,C).
draw(attr(node(n(R,C)), label, N)) :- pre(R,C,N).

#program frame.
shown(R,C) :- cand(num(R,C,_)).
draw(attr(node(n(R,C)), label, N)) :- cand(num(R,C,N)).
draw(ghost(node(n(R,C)))) :- cell(R,C), not shown(R,C), not pre(R,C,_), kind(_).
uses(a,E) :- cex(a(E)).
uses(b,E) :- cex(b(E)).
line(E,p(X1,Y1),p(X2,Y2)) :- ends(E,(X1,Y1),(X2,Y2)).
draw(attr(edge(P,Q), stroke, a)) :- line(E,P,Q), uses(a,E), not uses(b,E).
draw(attr(edge(P,Q), stroke, b)) :- line(E,P,Q), uses(b,E), not uses(a,E).
draw(attr(edge(P,Q), stroke, both)) :- line(E,P,Q), uses(a,E), uses(b,E).
draw(attr(edge(P,Q), weight, 10)) :- line(E,P,Q), uses(_,E).
draw(ghost(edge(P,Q))) :- line(E,P,Q), not uses(_,E), kind(_).
draw(note("Two loops fit the numbers: the edges of only a, only b, and both in three colours.")) :- kind(reject).
draw(note("One loop fits the numbers: the puzzle is done.")) :- kind(solution).
#show draw/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts: % A 7 x 7 puzzle with 12 numbers and a loop of at least 28 edges (about 6 s).

% Any loop length: the solver prefers small loops, which few numbers pin down
% (k = 10, under 2 s; with len = 28, k = 10 does not finish in two minutes).
% 5 x 5, 6 numbers, a loop of at least 16 edges.
% 10 x 10, 30 numbers, a loop of at least 50 edges (about 85 s).

% All 3 x 3 puzzles with 3 numbers and one solution (213 loops; checked by brute
% force over the cell sets that a loop encloses).
% All 4 x 4 puzzles with 3 numbers and one solution (9,349 loops; about 25 s).
% Two numbers never fix a loop on 4 x 4.

% Two corners print a 3; add two numbers (k = 2): 8 puzzles.
pre(1,1,3). pre(4,4,3).

% 4 x 4 with 4 numbers and a loop of at least 12 edges: 2,104 puzzles
% (about 6 minutes).

library.summary: A Slitherlink puzzle with a unique solution: one loop (reachability) and k numbers (7 x 7, 12 numbers, a loop of at least 28 edges; the run stops at the first puzzle).
